summary: This project explores the Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 spacecraft, launched by NASA in 1977, which are now abandoned in interstellar space. However, they are not forgotten. Each spacecraft carries a Golden Record containing images, natural sounds, music, and greetings in 55 languages from Earth. This project tells the story of these silent ambassadors to teenagers, explaining why NASA sent them and why they remain important symbols of human curiosity and hope.
details: Our project is a storytelling presentation (PDF) designed for school-age space enthusiasts. It introduces the Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 spacecraft, which NASA launched in 1977 and are now abandoned in interstellar space. The project tells the story of the Golden Records they carry, which contain images, natural sounds, music, and greetings in 55 languages from Earth. This project addresses the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge by explaining why this equipment was left behind, yet remains a vital symbol of human curiosity. The intended impact is to inspire teenagers to see space not as empty darkness, but as a place full of stories and hope. We used NASA's official data and image archives to gather the facts and visuals, and we designed the PDF using standard word processing software to ensure it is clear and engaging for a young audience.
